sections.title: 1. Introduction
sections.text_preview: This section introduces the System Requirements Specification (SRS) for Project ZNIX to its readers.

sections.title: 1.1 Purpose
sections.text_preview:
The purpose of this software requirements specification (SRS) is to establish the major requirements of the Project ZNIX research and development effort.

sections.title: 1.2 Scope
sections.text_preview: The SRS applies to the higher level design of the ZNIX Framework.

sections.title: 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms and Abbreviations

sections.title: 1.3.1 ZNIX
sections.text_preview: ZNIX is not an acronym. The term was decided upon to suggest the aspirant notion that a fully ZNIX integrated operating system could be the last (thus the letter “Z”) major evolution for POSIX system.

sections.title: 1.3.2 ZNIX Framework
sections.text_preview:

sections.text_preview: The Proxy Mechanism is the collection of Framework components that enable “ZNIX-unaware” applications to utilize the Framework capabilities.

sections.title: 3.3 Reliability
sections.text_preview: This subsection specifies the following requirements associated with the reliability of the system.

sections.title: 3.3.1 Mean Time between Failure (MTBF)
sections.text_preview: The mean time between failures (MTBF) SHALL exceed 3 months.

sections.title: 3.4.1 Capacity
sections.text_preview: At this stage of the development, the Framework MAY only operate in single user mode, with no networking capabilities.

sections.title: 3.4.2 Resource Utilization
sections.text_preview: The Framework Shell SHOULD NOT utilize more than 40 megabytes of RAM.

sections.title: 3.5.1 Coding Conventions
sections.text_preview: Any coding conventions to be used during implementation MUST be documented before the beginning of the phase, and strictly adhered to during the phase.

sections.title: 3.5.2 Compliance to Opens Source Standard Practices

sections.title: 3.6 Security
sections.text_preview:
The Framework MUST guard against malicious scripts on remote websites from accessing its information.

The Framework MUST guard against unintended corruption of information by the user himself.

sections.title: 3.7 Design Constraints
sections.text_preview: No design constraint has been imposed at this stage.
